messages:
sara: Anyone else seeing a spike of "partial_frame" errors from EU edge since last night? Console shows a bunch of ws_upgrade failures and small clients dropping mid-frame.
ben: Yea, started ~03:10 UTC. Symptoms: client sees socket close mid-message, server logs an incomplete_frame and closes the session. Not just one region but EU edges mostly.
priya: Any infra churn yesterday? I think cloud infra rolled a kernel/net tuning and our edge LB got a config push around 02:45 UTC.
sara: Log snippet I pulled from eu-edge-3 at 03:12:19:
```
[03:12:19.112] ws:upgrade incoming conn=abc123 remote=1.2.3.4
[03:12:19.116] ws:read error conn=abc123 err=read: connection reset by peer
[03:12:19.116] stream:incomplete_frame increment conn=abc123 frame_bytes=412 partial=true
[03:12:19.116] ws:close conn=abc123 reason=partial_frame
```
ben: Interesting that frame_bytes are small (~400B). Not a large chunking issue. I can repro locally with network throttling + `wscat`:
```
wscat -c wss://eu.redwood.ai/stream -H "x-client-id: test" --ping-interval 2000
# then trigger Chrome throttling or `tc qdisc` to add jitter
```
mike: deploy-bot shows a partial rollback/flip on the edge LB at 02:47:05 but the agent reports successful config apply at 02:50:02. That timing matches the spike.
priya: Hypothesis: proxy buffer/keepalive interplay. If the reverse proxy flushes or gets an early FIN while our websocket upgrade is streaming a small fragmented frame, our ws handler sees a zero-length read and treats it as a hard failure (counts incomplete_frame). Combined with some client throttling this leads to higher observed partial_frame counts.
ben: Proposed quick mitigation: treat a single `0-length read` during upgrade as transient, attempt a single non-blocking retry for the remaining bytes instead of immediate close. Patch sketched here: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/9876 (hotfix branch).
sara: :thumbsup: We should also add more telemetry tags so we can filter by `proxy_buffer_size` and `edge_lb_version`. Right now the metric doesn't carry those labels so debugging is noisy.
mike: I'll add a temporary alert and a console card. Alert (one-hour):
```
expr: sum(rate(stream_incomplete_frame_total{region="eu"}[5m])) by (edge_instance) > 3
for: 2m
```
priya: Also add `client_user_agent` and `net_throttle_flag` to the trace spans for 48h. We want to see if DevTools throttling or mobile carriers correlate.
sara: OK let's canary the `ws-upgrade-tolerate-zero-read` hotfix to eu-edge-canary. If we see duplicate-frame or reassembly regressions we rollback. Who owns rollback? @ben?
ben: I will own the rollback and watch the canary. I'll also add `stream_partial_frame_retries_total` to track retries.
deploy-bot: canary deploy: ws-upgrade-tolerate-zero-read -> eu-edge-canary (version 2026.03.21-rc1)
mike: For console UX: create a small card showing `stream_incomplete_frame_total` by `client_user_agent` and `edge_lb_version` so support can triage. Also add a one-click link from the metric to a pre-filtered trace view.
sara: Great. After 2 hours of canary we reconvene in #eng-platform. If the metric drops by 75% we promote. If duplicate frames > 1% we rollback immediately.
priya: Filed follow-ups: add buffer_size label to edge telemetry, add a test with induced small-frame jitter in our integration suite, and run a 6h soak with `tc` throttling.
sara: Thanks everyone, I'll note the action items in the rollout doc.
